samples.claim: try_infer_version considers all referenced_lance_files across fragments, including overlays. If no referenced file exists, returns Ok(None). Otherwise parses first exact version, then parses every file (including first again) and rejects any unequal ConcreteFileVersion with InvalidInput naming both versions. It ignores manifest mixed-version capability bits and does no IO. This strict helper is used for missing-format inference, not proof all supported manifests must be homogeneous.

samples.claim: Private false_positive_probability(ndv,log_space_bytes) implements the locally documented analytical model: bytes=2^log, ndv converted to f64; zero ndv returns0 and density ndv/(bytes*8)>2 returns1 early. Otherwise lambda=256/((bytes*8)/ndv), loglambda=ln(lambda). The u64 shift is used only at internal binary-search midpoints<64; this function does not itself validate arbitrary shift inputs. External paper attribution is not independently checked.

samples.claim: RangeWithHoles has start=1 inclusive, end=2 exclusive, and EncodedU64Array holes=3 storing sorted omitted values. samples.claim: ReserveFragments copies count. Rewrite prefers nonempty groups and ignores old flat fragment lists entirely; otherwise constructs exactly one RewriteGroup from old/new flat lists, even when both empty. Group conversion errors propagate before rewritten-index conversion. Rewritten indices convert from borrowed items; frag_reuse_index always None. Thus empty in-memory groups serialize empty and decode as one empty group, and transient reuse entry disappears; in-memory equality need not roundtrip. No merged history assembly occurs here.

samples.claim: CacheCodecImpl documentation explicitly marks serialized format experimental/no stability guarantee between releases, then describes future append-only TYPE_ID/protobuf field/enum rules and version bumps. Separate TYPE_ID docs below say must not change once shipped. Record this tension rather than inferring a released guarantee. Body serialization order and version-aware matching read order are implementor obligations; wrapper owns envelope only.

187 | // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
188 | // CacheCodecImpl — trait for serializable cache entry types
189 | // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
190 | 
191 | /// Serialization trait for cache entries.
192 | ///
193 | /// **Experimental**: the serialized format is not yet covered by a stability
194 | /// guarantee and may change between releases. When it does stabilize, the
195 | /// rules are: `TYPE_ID`, protobuf field numbers, and enum values are
196 | /// append-only forever; format changes that protobuf cannot express
197 | /// transparently bump [`CURRENT_VERSION`](Self::CURRENT_VERSION).
198 | ///
199 | /// Implement this on concrete types that need to survive serialization through
200 | /// a persistent cache backend, then wire it into a
201 | /// [`CacheKey`](super::CacheKey) via [`CacheCodec::from_impl`].
202 | ///
203 | /// The envelope (magic/version/type_id/type_version) is written and validated
204 | /// by the [`CacheCodec`] wrapper. [`serialize`](Self::serialize) writes only
205 | /// the body — a header followed by sections in a fixed, version-keyed order —
206 | /// and [`deserialize`](Self::deserialize) reads them back in that same order.
207 | /// The read sequence mirroring the write sequence for each `type_version` is
208 | /// the invariant the implementor owns.
samples.review_note: Experimental guarantee prose matches; supplemental209-225 confirms stronger once-shipped TYPE_ID wording and body-order obligation.
